sentences.text:
THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE R. NATARAJ  ORAL ORDER
In all these petitions, the petitioners have challenged the orders passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) impleading them as respondents.

2. The claimants in MVC Nos.03/2019, 3910/2019, 04/2019 and 1231/2019, all filed applications under Order I Rule 10 of CPC to implead the petitioners on the ground that these petitioners were charge sheeted by the police and some negligence was attributed to these petitioners that they were responsible for the accident which resulted in death and injury.
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:53162 AND 1 OTHER 3

. Learned counsel for the petitioners in all these writ petition contend that, the claim arises out of an accident which happened on a public road and the vehicles that were involved in the accident were duly insured.

She, therefore, contends that the petitioners cannot be proceeded against in an action under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, as liability to pay the compensation is only upon the insurer and no liability can be fastened upon the petitioners.

4. The learned counsel for the claimants on the other hand contended that, the police after investigating the accident had filed a charge sheet against the petitioners and it was found that the petitioners were responsible for the accident in some measure and therefore, the petitioners were sought to be brought on record in the claim petitions.
5. The claim petitions were filed claiming compensation from the owner and the insurer of the vehicle, which was responsible for the accident resulting in death and injury to certain persons.
The tribunal could determine the person liable to pay the compensation.

However, the Tribunal is not invested with the power to fasten liability on any person - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:53162 AND 1 OTHER other than the owner and the insurer of the vehicles involved in the accident.
Under the circumstances, these petitioners were neither proper nor necessary parties in a claim petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act.
The Trial Court, committed an error of sorts in allowing the applications and directed the impleadment of the petitioners herein.

Therefore, the impugned order is one passed without application of mind and therefore, warrants interference.
6.
Hence, these writ petitions are allowed.
The impugned orders are set aside and the applications filed by the claimants to implead the petitioners are all rejected.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
. Learned counsel for the petitioners in all these writ petition contend that, the claim arises out of an accident which happened on a public road and the vehicles that were involved in the accident were duly insured.
She, therefore, contends that the petitioners cannot be proceeded against in an action under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, as liability to pay the compensation is only upon the insurer and no liability can be fastened upon the petitioners.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However, the Tribunal is not invested with the power to fasten liability on any person - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:53162 AND 1 OTHER other than the owner and the insurer of the vehicles involved in the accident.
Under the circumstances, these petitioners were neither proper nor necessary parties in a claim petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, these writ petitions are allowed.
The impugned orders are set aside and the applications filed by the claimants to implead the petitioners are all rejected.
